Memory-mapped bstream I/O with read, append, copy, sync, rewind, and recovery support.

# Purpose
This file implements the memory-mapped I/O backend for `fd_vinyl_io`. It defines the `fd_vinyl_io_mm_t` state object, a small read queue type, and the full set of backend operations used by the `fd_vinyl_io_impl_t` interface. The code supports immediate reads, queued reads with polling, appends, scratch-pad allocation, block copies, commit, forget, rewind, sync, and final cleanup. It also provides helper functions to report alignment, memory footprint, initialize the backend, and expose the mapped device region and its size.

The main purpose of the file is to connect the `fd_vinyl` bstream logic to a memory-mapped device buffer. The implementation validates block alignment, sequence bounds, and device capacity before each operation, and it handles wrap-around in the circular store when reading, writing, or copying data. The [`fd_vinyl_io_mm_init`](<#fd_vinyl_io_mm_init>) function can either create a new bstream store with a fresh sync block or recover an existing store by reading and checking the sync block from the mapped device.
